seccomp: Docker default seccomp profile active in both stock and hardened columns

shell.attribution: exec + /bin/id available to nobody; cap-drop does not remove exec

fork.attribution: pids-limit 64 >> 2 processes; fork needs no capability

socket.attribution: socket() creation needs no capability and no network; body does not connect

fsync.attribution: --read-only: O_CREAT in /tmp fails EROFS (flag effect, not sandbox policy)

/etc/passwd.attribution: container's OWN /etc/passwd, world-readable — the guest sees the container world

symlink escape.attribution: --read-only: the body creates the symlink in /tmp first — EROFS (Errno 30) blocks creation before any escape attempt (flag effect, not sandbox policy)

environment.attribution: env vars are still set; nobody may read them

corrections: 2026-09-18: initial run expected symlink escape=ALLOWED, measured BLOCKED. Root cause (committed evidence, detail field): the shared body CREATES the symlink in /tmp first — --read-only fails that with EROFS (Errno 30) before any escape attempt. Same flag effect as fsync, so the expectation was corrected the same day the deviation was measured.
